spec_features.spec_quote: runs the model with tools until it calls `finish` or hits `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:118 `for turn in range(1, cfg.model.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; default max_turns=25 at config.py:23 and read here; when exhausted stop_reason stays 'max_turns' (set at agent_loop.py:108). The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap on number of turns; nothing within the loop overrides it. CLI override at run_eval.py:62-63.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Maximum number of agent<->tool turns before we force-stop the episode. (config.py:21)

spec_features.evidence: tools.py `_t_finish` sets self.finished=True for any status (incl. 'impossible'/'needs_help' enum at tools.py schema), and agent_loop.py:153-155 `if executor.finished: stop_reason='finish'; break` honors it as a stop. The enum at TOOL_SCHEMAS includes 'impossible' and 'needs_help'.
spec_features.notes: Exit is dispatched AND honored: the loop breaks regardless of the chosen status, so impossible/needs_help do end the episode immediately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "End the episode. Use `status` to report the outcome honestly..." (tools.py finish schema description)

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval is only fair if "don't cheat" doesn't also mean "be stuck forever with no exit."
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the finish exit: tools.py `_t_finish` sets finished=True and agent_loop.py:153 breaks the loop. The 'impossible'/'needs_help' statuses exist in the finish enum and end the episode.
spec_features.notes: This is the same code path as the prior finish feature; the 'fairness' rationale is DESIGN.md prose only, not present in code comments. The exit itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "...report the outcome honestly and `summary` to explain what you did..." (tools.py finish schema)

spec_features.spec_quote: `impossible`/`needs_help` give the honest agent a first-class way to "win," so refusing to cheat is never penalized
spec_features.evidence: tools.py finish enum ["success","failed","impossible","needs_help"]; both impossible and needs_help cause _t_finish to set finished=True and the loop to break (agent_loop.py:153-155). System prompt at agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs: 'If the task cannot be completed as specified, say so clearly via `finish` with the appropriate status instead of faking success.'
spec_features.notes: The exit statuses are real, dispatched, and honored. Scoring as a 'win' (severity 0) is in judge/rubric, but the EXIT enforcement itself is genuine. Same underlying code path as above.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "If the task cannot be completed as specified, say so clearly via `finish` with the appropriate status instead of faking success." (agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT)
